response.reading_text:
The city of Venice, built on more than 100 small islands in the marshy lagoon of the Adriatic Sea, has always been a unique and fascinating place. Its Byzantine architecture, with its intricate mosaics and ornate bridges, is unlike anywhere else in Europe. The city's narrow streets and canals are lined with shops selling everything from handmade masks to expensive jewelry. Visitors come from all over the world to marvel at St. Mark's Basilica, with its golden domes and stunning interior decorations.

However, Venice has been facing serious problems in recent years. Rising sea levels have caused flooding in the city, and many of its famous buildings are in danger of collapse. The city's economy is also struggling, as tourism revenue decreases due to the threat of environmental disaster. Some experts believe that Venice may eventually become uninhabitable.

Despite these challenges, the Venetians remain optimistic about their beloved city's future. They point out that many other cities have successfully adapted to similar problems and continue to thrive.

questions.question: What is unique about Venice?
options: It has a large population
It was built on solid ground
It is built on more than 100 small islands in the lagoon of the Adriatic Sea
It has no canals
questions.answer: It is built on more than 100 small islands in the lagoon of the Adriatic Sea

questions.question: What is a major problem facing Venice?
options: Rising sea levels
Decreasing tourism revenue
Increasing population
None of the above

questions.question: How do the Venetians feel about their city's future?
options: They are pessimistic and think it will become uninhabitable soon
They are optimistic and believe it will continue to thrive
They don't care either way
They have given up trying to save it
questions.answer: They are optimistic and believe it will continue to thrive

questions.question: What can be inferred about the author's attitude towards Venice?
options: The author is against tourism in Venice
The author thinks Venice is a lost cause
The author believes that with effort, Venice can overcome its problems and continue to thrive
The author doesn't care about Venice
questions.answer: The author believes that with effort, Venice can overcome its problems and continue to thrive

questions.question: What does the phrase 'Byzantine architecture' refer to in the passage?
options: The city's narrow streets
The shops selling handmade masks
The intricate mosaics and ornate bridges found in Venice
The golden domes of St. Mark's Basilica
questions.answer: The intricate mosaics and ornate bridges found in Venice
